case: A failed InnoDB DML batch rolls back transactional rows but preserves trigger writes to MyISAM and MEMORY tables
contract: An AFTER INSERT trigger writes each new ID to both MyISAM and MEMORY tables.
The batch inserts a new InnoDB parent row and then fails on a duplicate key; the InnoDB row is absent after rollback.
The trigger writes for the failed batch row remain in both non-transactional tables.
This establishes only these MySQL engine and trigger cases; it does not promise rollback atomicity across all engines or side effects.

focused_test.command: rtk proxy cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-mysql --test integration mysql_atomic::mysql_batch_rollback_does_not_claim_to_reverse_nontransactional_trigger_effects -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

format_and_diff.command: rtk cargo fmt --all -- --check; rtk git diff --check
